claim: mosquitto source (database.c db__message_write_queued_out): when a message fails both db__ready_for_flight and db__ready_for_queue, it is dropped with a one-time NOTICE log ('Outgoing messages are being dropped for client %s', latched by context->is_dropping), incrementing the publish_dropped counter and the client's messages_dropped stat — no error is sent to the subscriber.
stance_target: gap-07: the silent-drop mechanism confirmed in broker source code, independent of HA #135266
scope_conditions: mosquitto master (2026); db.c queue admission path
quoted_support: /* Dropping message due to full queue. */ if(context->is_dropping == false){ context->is_dropping = true; log__printf(NULL, MOSQ_LOG_NOTICE, "Outgoing messages are being dropped for client %s.", context->id); } metrics__int_inc(mosq_counter_mqtt_publish_dropped, 1); context->stats.messages_dropped++;

claim: Queue admission is PER-CLIENT and counts queued messages against max_queued_messages (default 1000): db__ready_for_queue computes valid_count = source_count - adjust_count < db.config->max_queued_messages on the client's own msg_data, and for a disconnected client the inflight adjustment zeroes out (adjust_count = 0 when !net__is_connected), making the full queue depth available to the offline replay.
stance_target: gap-07 sizing calibration: the binding quantity is per-client queued messages (not broker-wide retained inventory); at jupiterOS's ~25 agent entities the default 1000 is far from binding, so D9 lands as hygiene + $SYS monitoring, not urgent sizing
scope_conditions: mosquitto master source; QoS 1/2 or (QoS 0 with queue_qos0_messages)
quoted_support: valid_count = source_count - adjust_count < db.config->max_queued_messages; /* nothing in flight for offline clients */ if(!net__is_connected(context)){ adjust_bytes = 0; adjust_count = 0; }

claim: QoS 0 is NOT exempt from the queue cap: db__ready_for_flight's QoS-0 branch checks context->out_packet_count < db.config->max_queued_messages (outgoing direction) before delivering, so QoS-0 traffic to a slow reader — HA's '#' wildcard retained replay at QoS 0 in #135266 — is also bounded by max_queued_messages.
